prompt: On a cold morning a metal park bench and a wooden bench are both at exactly 10°C, yet the metal one feels much colder to sit on. Why?

options.text: The metal is actually at a lower temperature than the wood because it radiates more heat overnight
Metal conducts heat away from your warmer body much faster than wood does, so your skin cools faster where it touches metal
Wood generates a small amount of heat of its own, which metal cannot do
Metal feels colder only because it is smoother, so more of your skin touches it

explanation: How cold something feels depends on how fast it draws heat from your skin, not just its temperature. At the same 10°C, metal's high thermal conductivity pulls heat away quickly, while wood is a poor conductor and lets your skin stay warmer.
